user.title: PHASE Control — set up
user.description:
Name this room, then pick each zone's valve and probes and say how the room is plumbed. Watering stays off until you switch it on in PHASE Control, where everything else is set.

Running: **PHASE Control {version}**. {restart_notice}

data_description.name: What you call this room, e.g. 'Flower 2'. Shown on the dashboard; change it there any time.

data_description.room_name: A name for this grow room (e.g. Veg, Flower B). It gets its own zones, sensors, pump and setpoints, fully isolated from your other rooms.

data_description.num_zones: How many independent irrigation zones (valves) you control. You map each one's sensors next.

data_description.zone_1_switch: The switch entity that opens zone 1's irrigation valve.
data_description.zone_1_vwc: One or more substrate moisture (VWC) probes in zone 1. Choose several and the controller reads their average, until you choose otherwise in the zone's details on the dashboard. Outliers are not rejected automatically.
data_description.zone_1_ec: One or more substrate EC (pore-water) probes in zone 1, optional: the controller steers without them. Several are averaged, as the moisture probes are.

data_description.plumbing: What stands between the water and a zone valve. This is a statement about your plumbing, and the switches below have to match it. Setup refuses to save if they do not, and the controller refuses to water if they ever stop matching: a room that needs its pump is never run with the valve open and no pump. Not sure? If water only comes out while a pump is running, the room has a pump.
data_description.pump_switch: The switch that runs your water pump. Needed when the plumbing above includes a pump; leave it EMPTY when it does not (one switch per zone is the whole system, as in a tent on a smart plug, or the line is always under pressure). It is switched on its Pump Prime Time (2 seconds unless set) before a zone opens and off after it closes.
data_description.main_line_switch: The solenoid on the shared supply line feeding every zone; it opens its Main Line Lead Time (1 second unless set) before the zone valve. Needed when the plumbing above includes a main-line valve; leave it EMPTY when it does not.
data_description.lights_on_hour: Hour (0-23) the lights turn ON. Starts the grow-day; daily water/shot counters reset here.
data_description.lights_off_hour: Hour (0-23) the lights turn OFF. Forces every zone into the overnight dry-back phase (P3).

abort.use_dashboard: Those are set in PHASE Control, in Home Assistant's sidebar: each zone's name, plant count, pot size and drippers under Settings → Rooms & hardware, and its targets under Irrigation strategy → Today. Nothing was changed here.

kill_switch_missing.title: PHASE Control: kill switch helper missing (CS-601)
kill_switch_missing.description:
The engine is gated by the helper `input_boolean.f2_control_enabled`, but it doesn't exist, so the PHASE Controller app can't run. Create it: Settings → Devices & Services → Helpers → Create Helper → Toggle, named so the entity is input_boolean.f2_control_enabled. Leave it OFF until you're ready to irrigate.

Code CS-601. What it means and what to do: PHASE Control → Help → Error codes.

engine_offline.title: PHASE Control: engine not running (CS-602)
engine_offline.description:
No fresh heartbeat from the add-on (sensor.crop_steering_ai_heartbeat is missing or stale). The integration creates the entities, but the PHASE Controller app is what actually steers. Install/start it and check its log. If you only use manual control, you can ignore this.

Code CS-602. What it means and what to do: PHASE Control → Help → Error codes.

zone_no_sensor.title: PHASE Control: zone with no moisture sensor (CS-603)
zone_no_sensor.description:
Zone(s) {zones} have no VWC sensor mapped, so they can't be steered. Add a probe in Settings → Devices & Services → PHASE Control → Configure → Edit zones & hardware.

Code CS-603. What it means and what to do: PHASE Control → Help → Error codes.

fused_sensor_unavailable.title: PHASE Control: zone sensor unavailable (CS-604)
fused_sensor_unavailable.description:
The moisture sensor for zone(s) {zones} reads unavailable — the probe(s) may be offline or misnamed. Check it in Developer Tools → States and your zone mapping.

Code CS-604. What it means and what to do: PHASE Control → Help → Error codes.

strategy_hold.title: PHASE Control: irrigation strategy is holding its zones (CS-606)
strategy_hold.description:
The room's irrigation strategy is holding the steering of the zones it manages: {reason}. Until it clears, the controller waters those zones only with emergency and watchdog shots, and a zone with a dead probe on its timed schedule. See it in the PHASE Control panel under Irrigation strategy → Schedule. If it stays in error, fix the cause, then disarm the strategy and arm it again.

Code CS-606. What it means and what to do: PHASE Control → Help → Error codes.

strategy_degraded.title: PHASE Control: irrigation strategy has not moved on to today (CS-607)
strategy_degraded.description:
The room's irrigation strategy could not apply the current day at lights-on: {reason}. It keeps its last valid targets (a strategy waiting to start stays armed) and tries again every minute, and the controller keeps steering. This clears itself once the cause is fixed, usually a stale controller heartbeat or probe.

Code CS-607. What it means and what to do: PHASE Control → Help → Error codes.

entities_moved.title: PHASE Control: {count} setting(s) are not where the controller looks for them (CS-605)
entities_moved.description:
The controller finds each setting by its exact entity id, and these are somewhere else, so it is running on its built-in defaults for them (daily water cap and plant count included):

{entities}

Keep the engine off until this is fixed. If you changed an entity id yourself, change it back: Settings → Devices & services → Entities → the entity → the cog → Entity ID. If nearly every entity is listed, the room was created while Home Assistant was still running an older version of this integration: delete the PHASE Control entry, restart Home Assistant, and add it again. Nothing is renamed for you, because an id you chose on purpose is yours to keep.

Code CS-605. What it means and what to do: PHASE Control → Help → Error codes.

stock_low.title: PHASE Control: {count} stock tank(s) running low (CS-608)
stock_low.description:
These stock tanks are at or below their low mark:

{tanks}
